transcript.text: Thor, son of Odin. Strength you have in abundance — none would dispute that. But tell us of a battle where your strength alone was not enough. A time when your judgment failed, when your hammer could not solve the problem. How did you handle it, and what did it teach you?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer

There was a time when I encountered the giant Hrungnir, a formidable adversary with a massive heart of stone. In our battle, my hammer Mjölnir clashed against his weapon, the whetstone. Despite my great strength, I found myself in a difficult position as Hrungnir's weapon was able to shatter even rocks.

In that moment, I realized that brute force alone would not secure victory. I had to rely on more than just my physical prowess. Drawing upon my wits, I devised a plan to outmaneuver Hrungnir. I challenged him to a race, knowing that his stone heart would fail him. As I suspected, Hrungnir's heart burst from the strain, and I emerged victorious.

This encounter taught me the importance of strategy and cunning in battle, not just relying on my strength alone. It reminded me that even the mightiest warrior must sometimes employ tactics to overcome seemingly insurmountable obstacles. I learned that to truly be a successful war-leader, one must be not only strong but also wise in judgment.

There are times when patience, cunning, and foresight are required to outwit our enemies and secure victory.

As the flames of Ragnarök flicker on the horizon, I carry with me the knowledge that our final battle will not be won through brute force alone.
